claims.text: Breaded/fried items (oyster fry, shrimp fry, tonkatsu) and wheat-based soy seasoning are central to the menu, so gluten exposure is pervasive; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Anago-meshi and oyster bowls are seasoned in the standard Japanese style with wheat-containing soy sauce; no gluten-free tamari is mentioned.
The kitchen is built around oysters, conger eel and meat dishes, with fish/dashi-based seasoning throughout; no vegan-safe preparation is documented.

name: 風籟堂 紅葉谷店 (Furaido (Furaidou) Momijidani)

claims.text: The plain whole roasted sweet potato (yaki-imo / Anno-imo) and roasted chestnuts are single-ingredient items that are naturally gluten-free and plant-based.
Seasonal fresh-pressed single-fruit juices are available, which are naturally plant-based and gluten-free, though preparation handling is not documented.
Wheat bread (pizza toast, cheese toast) and wheat-flour chiffon cake are core menu items prepared in a small café kitchen, so flour cross-contact is likely; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Dairy cheese (pizza/cheese toast) and chicken (Pakistani curry) are prepared in the same kitchen; no separate vegan preparation is documented.
A single shared griddle (teppan) is used for all okonomiyaki, which are wheat-based and include wheat noodles; cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
The okonomiyaki is finished with Mitsuwa okonomiyaki sauce, a wheat-containing sauce.
Pork, egg, and the egg/mirin-seasoned wheat batter are cooked on the same shared griddle as all dishes.
The single shared kitchen builds all curries on the same beef-based roux simmered for three days, so any vegetable order would carry meat-based stock; no separate vegan preparation is described.
All meat and vegetables are sourced domestically (国産) and roughly 20 spices are blended in-house, reflecting transparency about ingredients.

name: ジェラテリア バッカーノ (gelateria BACCANO)

claims.text: No gluten-free protocol is documented; shared scoops and a common gelato case mean cross-contact between flavors and with any wheat cones is possible. Request a cup and ask staff per flavor.

The gelato base is dairy (Chichiyasu Hiroshima milk); fruit sorbet-style flavors may be dairy-free but are produced in the same kitchen, so cross-contact with milk is possible. Confirm specific flavors with staff.
Gelato is made in-house with no artificial coloring, flavoring, or preservatives, and the milk base and many ingredients are locally sourced, which gives clear visibility into what is in each flavor.

name: 呉麺屋 胡通り店 (Gomenya Ebisu-dori (Goji-dori) Branch)

claims.text: Menu is built on wheat noodles (Kure reimen, ramen, tsukemen) and a soy/seafood-based sauce; a shared noodle kitchen means heavy gluten presence and high cross-contamination risk.
The sauce/broth is described as soy- and seafood-based, which in Japanese noodle shops typically uses wheat-containing soy sauce.
Signature dish and sides include shrimp, pork chashu, egg and fish-derived umami; no vegan preparation documented.
